title: Superman Review: James Gunn's Fresh Take With David Corenswet Is The Reboot DC Needed
text:
Superman Review: James Gunn’s Fresh Take With David Corenswet Is The Reboot DC Needed
James Gunn’s attempt at reviving DC is a decent watch that will hopefully give DC Universe the much-needed momentum to build on.
David Corenswet makes his appearance as the new Superman in the DC Comic universe. (Photo Credits: Instagram) David Corenswet makes his appearance as the new Superman in the DC Comic universe. (Photo Credits: Instagram)
SupermanU
Watch Trailer
Superman Review: James Gunn’s reboot of DC Comics’ Superman was probably the much-needed reintroduction of the iconic superhero that made us fall in love with the Big Blue. However, the director has chosen to sidestep the original story. The film starts where David Corenswet has been established on Earth for the last 30 years and has established himself as Clark Kent / Superman. The setting of the movie will give you a mixed vibe where you are immersed in a retro yet futuristic Metropolis. Corenswet is joined by Krypto, the super dog, who adds the much-needed laughter occasionally in the movie.
Gunn is clear in his approach with the film and doesn’t take the Zack Snyder route and makes the screenplay a serious tale of events. Gunn has added a few laughs and some quite a few surprise elements that is bound to bring a smile to your face. The element of surprise starts from seeing Bradley Cooper as Jor-El, Superman’s biological father. The actor has made an appearance only through an AI video message that plays out in the film. Besides this, there are two more cameos in the film by John Cena and Sean Gunn. Do not blink, as you might just miss these two in different scenes throughout the film.
Recommended Stories
All said and done, let’s address the elephant in the room. David Corenswet makes his appearance as the new Superman in the DC Comics universe. The actor brings the old-school charm as the big blue. His physique, style of acting, and dialogue delivery all convince you to believe Corenswet is the iconic superhero we need. The actor looks sharp in the red cape, but makes you want to see him in action a lot more than what has been showcased in the film. The story highlights the emotional turmoil Superman goes through in his life when he discovers the second half of the message his parents had for him recorded in the videotape. And Corenswet has mastered the right emotions of the superhero and what makes him a “human" more than an “alien".
As much as you appreciate Corenswet’s debut as the Big Blue, one cannot ignore the efforts put in by Nicholas Hoult as Lex Luthor. He is a cold-blooded, intelligent and a smart villain who is on a mission to kill Superman. Hoult has done a good job in portraying his character and the bald look kind of suits him, too. Another significant performance is that of Rachel Brosnahan, who plays Lois Lane in the film. Broshnahan will convince you that she is indeed the feisty journalist in real life as well. Besides, the film sees Nathan Fillion, Isabela Merced and Edi Gathegi in vital roles as the Justice Gang, who help out Superman in this battle.
The action sequences in the film could have been a little more impactful and edgy. However, it doesn’t disappoint when it comes to the main climax fight sequences that unfolds between Ultraman and Superman. Though you may feel the first half of the film lacks the intensity and the pace, the storytelling surely improves in the second half, making it a lot more edgy as a superhero movie should be. Overall, James Gunn’s attempt at reviving DC is a decent watch that will hopefully give DC Universe the much-needed momentum to build on.
